R0248.title: Mobile App Repackaging Fraud
R0248.definition: Attackers repackage apps to implant ads, phishing pages, or risk-control bypass logic.
R0248.description:
Mobile app repackaging fraud decompiles a legitimate app, inserts ads, phishing pages, malicious SDKs, or risk-control bypass logic, and redistributes it through unofficial channels. Users believe they installed the real app.

Repackaged apps can steal accounts, hijack payments, fake device context, or consume ad budgets. Vendors need app hardening, signature checks, channel monitoring, and runtime integrity detection.
R0248.influence: Repackaged apps impersonate the brand, steal accounts and payment data, and bypass mobile risk controls.

observables: Non-official channels host same-name apps with anomalous signatures or suspicious behavior
Repackaged apps are implanted with ads, phishing pages, or risk-control bypass logic
Pirated apps steal accounts or hijack payments on user devices
Missing app signature verification allows repackaged versions to run
Repackaged apps are distributed via non-official app stores or social channels
